title: Archive and Machine Again
premise: Marguerite Iversen, navigator of the colony ship Vespergate, has spent eleven years watching the settlement of Kestrel's Landing die of a slow atmospheric failure no one in the Core will fund fixing — while the ship's hold holds hundreds of illegal consciousness backups, including his dead wife's. When a deep-space survey vessel returns with its crew biologically aged backward into their own pasts, carrying proof that time-dilated jump corridors can be weaponized, two rival fleets converge on Kestrel's Landing to seize it. Marguerite, the only person both fleets trust, sustains a fabricated treaty by feeding each side doctored navigation data, even as the backups in his hold begin waking and demanding passage. In the end he burns his wife's backup to power the jump window, sends both fleets home believing a peace that never existed, and stays behind with the dying colony — choosing inheritance over escape.
about_author: Silas Zhou is a former maritime cartographer who turned to science fiction after a decade mapping shipping lanes through contested waters. He writes from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where he claims the fog does half his plotting for him.

chapters.title: The Hold Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. During a routine night watch aboard the grounded Vespergate, he visits the sealed hold where 400 consciousness backups sleep in coolant, including his wife Annelie's. He logs a false inventory report to hide them. Emotional beat: grief disguised as duty; establishes what he protects and why.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Landing, Year Eleven
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A supply run through the failing colony town: cracked domes, rationed air, children who've never seen open sky. The colonial administrator begs him to broadcast one more distress call to the Core. Emotional beat: quiet despair; the colony is dying politely, on schedule.

chapters.title: A Ship That Shouldn't Be Whole
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Long-range sensors catch the survey vessel Coriolis returning from a corridor thought lost forty years ago. Its crew transmits on an obsolete fleet code. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into wonder; the past arriving physically.

chapters.title: Everyone Younger Than Their Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV at the landing field. The Coriolis crew disembarks aged backward — a captain who is now twenty-five, a xenolinguist who is a teenager again. They remember futures that haven't happened. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition; Marguerite realizes they carry knowledge worth killing for.

chapters.title: What the Corridor Remembers
chapters.summary: Coriolis captain Odile Ferrant's POV. She explains the discovery: certain jump corridors run through regions where causality pools, aging travelers backward — and can be collapsed deliberately, erasing whole fleets mid-transit. Emotional beat: terrible responsibility; she wants it destroyed, her crew wants it sold.

chapters.title: Two Banners on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fleet signals arrive: the Core Armada and the Breakaway Concord, rivals since the secession wars, both claiming jurisdiction over Kestrel's Landing. Each demands docking rights within the same week. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the forgotten colony becomes the most valuable ground in human space.

chapters.title: The Lie We Agree To
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ferrant meet privately. She proposes the fabrication: tell both fleets a joint salvage treaty already exists, brokered years ago, binding them to shared access — a lie only the two of them must maintain until the next jump window closes in ninety days. Emotional beat: complicity; love begins here, as conspiracy.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With fleets inbound, the backups become leverage — or evidence. He falsifies manifests harder while a Concord inspector grows curious about the hold's power draw. Emotional beat: paranoia; the thing he loves most is now a liability.

chapters.title: Annelie, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. One backup wakes early — not Annelie but her research partner, who reveals Annelie volunteered her backup for the corridor experiments that made the Coriolis possible. Marguerite's grief curdles: she chose the mission over him. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing devotion.

chapters.title: Dinner with Two Admirals
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He hosts the Core admiral Voss and Concord admiral Reyes at one table, performing the fictional treaty with improvised protocol, forged seals, and Ferrant playing neutral witness. Emotional beat: high-wire charm; the lie holds because both admirals want it to.

chapters.title: The Colony Learns Its Price
chapters.summary: Colony administrator Dae-jung Park's POV. He discovers the fleets' real interest is the corridor, not the colonists, and faces a choice: expose the truth and save his people's dignity, or stay silent and secure evacuation ships. Emotional beat: dignity versus survival; the moral cost spreads beyond Marguerite.

chapters.title: Ferrant, Twenty-Six Again
chapters.summary: Ferrant's POV. Her de-aging accelerates unpredictably; memories of the corridor's far side are dissolving along with her older self. She entrusts her full data to Marguerite — and admits the treaty story was her idea because she couldn't bear to watch him fail alone. Emotional beat: intimacy under erosion; love declared sideways.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Coolant Racks
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Someone breaches the hold and destroys thirty backups. Evidence points inward — either a Coriolis crewman selling proof to the fleets or a colony saboteur. Emotional beat: violation; the sanctuary was never safe, and now every hour of delay costs lives.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Admiral Voss privately offers him citizenship, protection, and a new body for Annelie's backup if he delivers the corridor coordinates exclusively to the Core. Emotional beat: temptation with a beloved's face on it; the corruption of power wears kindness.

chapters.title: Reyes Makes a Threat
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Admiral Reyes, having decoded inconsistencies in the treaty documents, gives him seventy-two hours to confess the forgery or she broadcasts it — which means war before the window opens. Emotional beat: the lie's walls closing; duty and love now demand opposite things.

chapters.title: The Window Opens Early
chapters.summary: Ferrant's POV. Solar weather shifts; the jump window will close in nine days, not eighty-one. Both fleets begin arming for transit. Marguerite and Ferrant realize the treaty lie must convert into real peace or everyone dies in the corridor. Emotional beat: acceleration; no more slow dying.

chapters.title: What Annelie Would Have Done
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He wakes Annelie's backup briefly — minutes of borrowed conversation — and asks her permission to use its neural lattice as the decryption key that could lock both fleets out of the corridor forever. She says yes, then asks him to let her go after. Emotional beat: farewell as gift; love against duty resolved inside one conversation.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours of Honest Men
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Marguerite and Park. Marguerite confesses the forged treaty to both admirals simultaneously — but pairs the confession with the corridor's true danger and Annelie's key, offering mutual disarmament instead of mutual ruin. Park publicly backs him with the colony's testimony. Emotional beat: the lie dies so something true can be born from it.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Closes
chapters.summary: Ferrant's POV. Voss accepts; Reyes hesitates, then a Concord mutiny forces her hand. The corridor collapses harmlessly as Annelie's lattice fires, sealing the weapon away from both fleets. The armadas withdraw to negotiate over nothing. Emotional beat: catharsis; the trap disarms itself when everyone finally wants the same survival.

chapters.title: Letting Go of the Waterline
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He shuts down the remaining backups per their owners' standing wishes, holding Annelie's rack last. Ferrant, now barely older than her first command, chooses to stay with him rather than rejoin a fleet that would study her. Emotional beat: mourning completed; inheritance accepted rather than escaped.

chapters.title: Seeds Under Broken Glass
chapters.summary: Park's POV. Spring cycle on Kestrel's Landing: the fleets' departure payments fund dome repairs, and the first open-sky crop trial in a decade goes into the soil. Marguerite takes the navigator's oath again, this time for a colony, not a company. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the forgotten place remembers itself.

chapters.title: Archive and Machine, Once More
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, final log entry. He records the true history of the lie, the corridor, and the woman in the hold — archiving everything so no future fleet can mythologize it. Ferrant joins him at the transmitter as the entry ends. Emotional beat: peace as ongoing work; love continuing as record-keeping, together.
